ui_bugs.issue: Employee login is blocked by browser HTML5 validation. The email field is <Input type='email' required> so entering username 'aliusta' triggers 'Please include an @ in the email address' and the form never submits. Backend accepts username in the email field (verified via API), but the UI login flow for employees is broken. Fix: change type='email' to type='text' (and drop the Mail icon rename), or add noValidate to the form.

action_items: Fix StudioPortal.jsx: change studio-email input type from 'email' to 'text' (or add form noValidate) so employees can log in with a plain username per spec ('put the username in the email field').
Optional: suppress benign 401 console noise on /studyo/* pages (main-site axios calls notifications/bell endpoints that don't accept studio_token) — non-blocking, flagged in iter 34 as well.

rca of the issue: StudioPortal login uses HTML5 email validation on the shared login/register form. When employees enter their username (non-email) in the email field, the browser rejects submission before the app can call /api/studio/login. Fix: switch to type='text' or add noValidate to the form; backend already supports both email and username identifiers.
